subject: zoology_2
question_text: Define the terms layer and broiler.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.58, VSAQ 126. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): step 2's margin note called the age an extra point while its second mistake called leaving the age out an error; the note now says the age is an extra detail and the mistake was replaced, since 'a bird raised only for meat' is already a complete definition.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Layer
steps.why: A bird kept for eggs is fed and housed to lay for as long as possible.
common_mistakes: Saying layers are raised for meat.
lines: Layers are birds which are exclusively
raised for the production of eggs.

steps.label: Broiler
steps.why: A bird kept for meat is grown fast and sold young, so it never reaches laying age.
common_mistakes: Defining a broiler only by its age. The definition is a bird raised for meat.
steps.memory_tip: Broilers are raised for meat and sold at 8 to 10 weeks.
steps.margin_note: Give the meaning first. The age is a useful extra detail, not part of the definition.
lines: Broilers are birds which are raised only for

lines.text: They are raised up to 8 or 10 weeks, then sold

insider_note: This question is asked more often than any other two-mark question in this chapter. One word each decides the mark: eggs for layers, meat for broilers.
